response.sql:
WITH total_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM orderexecutions
),
execution_stats AS (
  SELECT
    ordersmark,
    COUNT(*) as execution_count,
    CAST(COUNT(*) AS DECIMAL) / CAST((SELECT total FROM total_count) AS DECIMAL) as share
  FROM orderexecutions
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
avg_share_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM execution_stats
),
with_diff AS (
  SELECT
    es.ordersmark,
    es.execution_count,
    es.share,
    es.share - asc.avg_share as diff
  FROM execution_stats es
  CROSS JOIN avg_share_calc asc
)
SELECT
  ordersmark,
  execution_count,
  share,
  diff
FROM with_diff
ORDER BY
  ordersmark IS NULL ASC,
  diff DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The average share is computed across all order references including the NULL group (executions lacking a reference). The NULL ordersmark group is treated as one valid order reference per the request's specification.
DECIMAL division is used to preserve full precision without rounding. The division CAST(COUNT(*) AS DECIMAL) / CAST(total AS DECIMAL) ensures decimal arithmetic across database systems.

Missing values (NULL ordersmark) appear at the end of the sorted result set, regardless of their difference values. Non-NULL rows are listed first (sorted by difference descending), followed by the NULL group.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share excludes the NULL ordersmark group, computing the average only across non-NULL order references. This would treat 'order reference' as inherently non-NULL values only.
